name: West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc. (WST)
analyst_actions: 2026-07-24 | Bank of America Securities | reiterates Buy | 410.0->410.0
product: High-Value Product Components (Westar, NovaPure, Envision, Daikyo Crystal Zenith closures and vials) for biologics and GLP-1 elastomers, plus HVP Delivery Devices (self-injection, SmartDose on-body). HVP Components were $424.1M, +19.4%, and HVP Delivery Devices $131.2M, +29.6%, in Q2 2026 (2026-07-23).
demand: Mix-led. Q2 2026 growth came from the HVP mix shift (Annex 1 upgrades), GLP-1 volume and a Europe production ramp; gross margin rose to 37.7% from 35.7% (2026-07-23). No evidence of net price increases; Standard Products grew only +0.7% organic.
pricing_power: A mix reversal would compress the 37.7% gross margin: Standard Products (+0.7% organic) or West Vantage (+0.8%) growing faster than HVP, failure to hold HVP pricing, or lost GLP-1 volume (2026-07-23). Cyber-incident costs and SmartDose deal charges are one-offs, not recurring (2026-07-23).
competition: Chinese and Indian elastomer closures, vials and prefilled syringes are cheaper, but not close for regulated high-value biologics: Annex 1, FDA and EMA quality and change-control barriers protect West's position (2026-07-23). No specific substitute named in the sources read.
market_strategy: CEO Eric M. Green, 2026-07-23: FY26 net sales $3.345-3.380B, organic +10-11%, adjusted EPS $8.85-9.05; Q3 net sales $820-835M and adjusted EPS $2.14-2.24. Earlier, 2026-02-12: FY26 net sales $3.215-3.275B and adjusted EPS $7.85-8.20, assuming a mid-2026 SmartDose 3.5mL close.
bull: Q2 2026 (2026-07-23): organic +12.7%, HVP Components +19.4%, Delivery Devices +29.6%, gross margin 37.7% vs 35.7%; FY26 guidance raised twice; six firms raised targets in 90 days.
bear: Q3 2026 reported growth guided +1.9-3.8% as SmartDose drops out; Standard Products only +0.7% organic, so mix reversal would compress margin; May 2026 cyberattack cost still unquantified.
falsifier: Q3 2026 earnings: reported net sales growth below 1.9% year over year, or organic growth below the guided +7.0-8.9%, or an FY26 guidance cut.
web_what_changed_30_90d: Last 90 days: FY26 guidance raised twice, Q1 on 2026-04-23 and Q2 on 2026-07-23 to net sales $3.345-3.380B and adjusted EPS $8.85-9.05; Q2 organic +12.7% (2026-07-23); Daikyo crosslicense amended 2026-07-14; material May 2026 cyberattack disclosed 2026-05-11. Last 30 days: no new primary event; only routine company X posts (2026-09-23 to 2026-09-26).
web_true_now_not_modelled: Models may under-read that Q3 2026 reported growth compresses to +1.9-3.8% only because SmartDose 3.5mL ($30M in Q3 2025) is stripped out, while underlying organic is guided +7.0-8.9% (2026-07-23). The May 2026 cyberattack impact on financials remains undetermined (2026-05-11), an unmodelled tail risk.
web_demand_product: High-Value Product Components (Westar, NovaPure, Envision, Daikyo Crystal Zenith closures and vials) for biologics and GLP-1 elastomers, plus HVP Delivery Devices (self-injection, SmartDose on-body). HVP Components were $424.1M, +19.4%, and HVP Delivery Devices $131.2M, +29.6%, in Q2 2026 (2026-07-23).
web_price_volume_mix: Mix-led. Q2 2026 growth came from the HVP mix shift (Annex 1 upgrades), GLP-1 volume and a Europe production ramp; gross margin rose to 37.7% from 35.7% (2026-07-23). No evidence of net price increases; Standard Products grew only +0.7% organic.
web_bottleneck: West's own constraint is elastomer/component capacity and Annex 1 quality-compliance ramp, especially Europe. It relieves biopharma container-closure and fill-finish bottlenecks (particulate, endotoxin, high-viscosity) that gate GLP-1 and biologic supply (2026-07-23; X 2026-09-25).
web_who_benefits_next: Second-order: fill-finish CDMOs, GLP-1 and biologic drugmakers, self-injection device integrators, and 49%-owned Daikyo, plus glass and primary-packaging suppliers whose volumes West's components pull (2026-07-23).
web_who_loses: Rival containment and delivery suppliers: Aptar, Stevanato Group, Gerresheimer, SCHOTT Pharma in vials and prefilled syringes, and BD's syringe unit. Named in sources: West gives up the SmartDose 3.5mL stream to AbbVie, $55M in H2 2025 and $30M in Q3 2025, now excluded from organic growth (2026-07-23).
web_margin_collapse_risk: A mix reversal would compress the 37.7% gross margin: Standard Products (+0.7% organic) or West Vantage (+0.8%) growing faster than HVP, failure to hold HVP pricing, or lost GLP-1 volume (2026-07-23). Cyber-incident costs and SmartDose deal charges are one-offs, not recurring (2026-07-23).
web_low_cost_substitute: Chinese and Indian elastomer closures, vials and prefilled syringes are cheaper, but not close for regulated high-value biologics: Annex 1, FDA and EMA quality and change-control barriers protect West's position (2026-07-23). No specific substitute named in the sources read.
web_ceo_promised: CEO Eric M. Green, 2026-07-23: FY26 net sales $3.345-3.380B, organic +10-11%, adjusted EPS $8.85-9.05; Q3 net sales $820-835M and adjusted EPS $2.14-2.24. Earlier, 2026-02-12: FY26 net sales $3.215-3.275B and adjusted EPS $7.85-8.20, assuming a mid-2026 SmartDose 3.5mL close.
web_did_they_deliver: Yes so far. Q1 2026 organic +15.3% (2026-04-23) and Q2 2026 organic +12.7% (2026-07-23), both above the initial roughly 5-7% plan; guidance raised at both prints; FY2025 free cash flow $468.9M, +69.6% (2026-02-12).
web_what_would_falsify: Q3 2026 reported net sales growth below 1.9% year over year, or an FY26 guidance cut, disclosed on the Q3 2026 earnings date; also organic growth below the guided +7.0-8.9% for Q3, or a quantified material financial hit from the May 2026 cyberattack (2026-05-11).
